rationale: Recurrent verb in this kephalaion (lines 3, 4, 6, 30) of archonic violent contact with their targets, in parallel with ⲧⲱⲙⲧ 'reach upon' and ⲧⲉⲍⲁϩ 'reach.' The reduplicated form ⲟⲁⲙⲟⲙ may intensify ('smite repeatedly') or be a morphological variant. Etymology uncertain. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.

Plural noun paired with ⲛⲓⲍⲣⲟⲩⲙⲡⲉ 'the thunders' (line 21) in cloud-meteorological context. Likely a Lycopolitan term for lightning, possibly related to ⲉⲃⲣⲏϭⲉ. Distinct from the cosmological 'fruit/seed-fruit' homograph.

Variant orthography of accumulated ⲉⲃⲣⲏⲩⲉ 'fruits/seed-fruits.' Used with ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ and ⲧⲱⲟⲉ in line 28 — agricultural-destructive context confirms the harvest sense. In line 1 the archons 'strip the fruits' as part of their destructive activity.
Lycopolitan compound ⲥⲙ- (= ⲥⲙⲟⲧ 'form, manner') + ⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness'). Identifying noun used in formula 'the form is that of X.' Distinct from ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness' alone.

Cold-weather noun paired in inventory with ⲭⲁⲗⲁⲍⲁ 'hail' (χάλαζα) and ⲭⲓⲱⲛ 'snow' (χιών). Likely Lyc reflex of native Coptic ϫⲁϥ 'frost.' The triple inventory frost/hail/snow describes the archons' destructive winter precipitation.

In line 28 paired agriculturally with ⲛⲃⲣⲏⲟⲩⲉ 'seed-fruits' and ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'fruits' as the destruction-objects of winter weather. Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲧⲟⲉ 'produce, crops' (cf. accumulated ⲛ̄†ⲟⲉ 'the crops'); alternative reading 'mountains' (cf. ⲧⲱⲟⲥ in glossary) less suited to context.
Habitual negative ⲙⲁⲩ-ⲣ̄-ⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲛ 'they habitually do no good' with Greek loanword ἀγαθόν and Lyc ⲫ for ⲑ. With ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'ever' = 'they are never beneficial.' Standard Coptic + Greek-loan composite.

proposed_english: at their feet / stand at their feet
rationale: Lyc compound preposition ϩⲓⲣⲁⲧ⸗ 'at the foot of' with 3pl suffix (cf. accumulated ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧϩ̄ 'at the foot of'). With ⲣ̄- prefix in line 6 = 'shall stand at their feet' (with ⲛⲁ- future).
